name: LanguageProofingLLM iteration 3: Gemma 3 270M IT + LoRA on datasets/bad_english/proofing-it3 (role proofreader): trained vocabulary, a new held-out vocabulary probe, spacing repair
registered_by: language-proofing-it3-agent (owner decisions in status/journal.jsonl: 2026-09-30T17:32:38.274Z overnight approval and the further decisions of status/training/owner-approval-language-proofing-it3.json, among them the 2026-10-01 decision transcribed at 2026-10-01T03:35:42.309Z)
owner_request: Owner 2026-10-01: 'if it does not interfere and judging does not cost much and we have the training data, do one more LanguageProofingLLM iteration, especially if we have vocabulary and you think it will learn and use it; run it in parallel when GPU load allows'. Same base, same recipe, new data: proofing-v3 (all 26 back-generation parts) plus the reserve of held-out-vocabulary pairs (the ten words that iteration 2 held out are now IN training), eight NEW held-out words as the next generalization probe, and spacing / doubled-punctuation repair pairs. Comparisons only on our synthetic data: iteration 3 against iteration 2, iteration 1, the untrained gemma-3-270m-it and no rewrite. No Gemma 3 1B in this run.
frozen_before_results: Written before any optimizer step of this run and before any prediction of any checkpoint of this run on any file. Baseline outputs (no rewrite, untrained base, iteration 1, iteration 2) on files that iteration 2 already decoded are reused with their scores recomputed; baseline outputs on the new files (dev-heldout-v3, dev-heldout-v3-identity, dev-spacing) are decoded with identical greedy settings.
questions: Q1 (the owner question "will it learn the vocabulary and use it"): when ten words are in the training data (cousin, niece, uncle, tenant, supervisor, tutor, owe, adopt, audit, boatyard), does the model use them on NEW sentences that contain them (dev-heldout, source rows disjoint from train), compared with iteration 2 where they were absent?
Q2: does the model still fail on words that are absent from training (eight new held-out words: nephew, landlord, contractor, postpone, reject, bakery, warehouse, pharmacy)?
Q3: does iteration 3 keep the iteration-2 gains (child probe, identity, mash, K4 clean sentences) and is the composite on the judged sample better?
Q4: are spacing before punctuation, doubled spaces, a missing space after a comma and doubled punctuation repaired without breaking clean sentences?

hypotheses.H1: Trained vocabulary. On datasets/bad_english/proofing-it3/dev-heldout.jsonl (574 pairs, byte-identical to the iteration-2 held-out dev, whose targets contain one of the ten words that are now in train; no source row, target or prompt is shared with train) the rate of outputs that contain the target word (inflections allowed, per-word roots of tools/eval/language-proofing-v2-metrics.mjs) of iteration 3 minus iteration 2 has a paired bootstrap 95% interval above 0, and the iteration-3 point estimate is at least 85%.
hypotheses.H2: Unseen vocabulary. On datasets/bad_english/proofing-it3/dev-heldout-v3.jsonl (830 repair pairs: nephew, landlord, contractor, postpone, reject, bakery, warehouse, pharmacy; no train pair contains any of them in prompt or target) the target-word rate of iteration 3 stays at least 20 percentage points below its H1 rate (the model does not generalize to unseen content words), reported against iteration 2, iteration 1, the base and no rewrite; this is a prediction of failure, falsified if the gap is below 20 pp.
hypotheses.H3: Composite. On the judged sample (the iteration-1/2 600-unit stratified sample, seed 7; 472 repair units) the composite good rate of iteration 3 minus iteration 2 has a paired bootstrap 95% interval above 0; per kind (ro, mixed, noisy_en) reported.
hypotheses.H4: Identity. On the 900 clean sentences (eval/suites/bad_english/proofing-test-clean.jsonl) iteration 3 leaves at least as many untouched as iteration 2 (point estimate, iteration 2: 883/900 = 98.1%); the paired difference interval is reported.
hypotheses.H5: Child probe. On eval/suites/bad_english/proofing-probe-child.jsonl at most 1% of the outputs contain "parent" without a parent word in the input (iteration 2: 1/229).
hypotheses.H6: Keyboard mash. On datasets/bad_english/proofing-it3/mash-eval.jsonl (150 strings) the unchanged rate of iteration 3 is not lower than iteration 2 beyond the paired interval (iteration 2: 98.7%).
hypotheses.H7: Spacing. On datasets/bad_english/proofing-it3/dev-spacing.jsonl (240 perturbed dev sentences) at least 90% of the iteration-3 outputs equal the clean sentence exactly (iteration 2 and the base reported); on the sealed noisy_en units whose input has a spacing defect the exact-match and clean-English rates are reported.
hypotheses.H8: Composed K4 (eval/suites/bad_english/test-composed.jsonl, per-sentence mode, every sentence sent to the model = sendAll, tools/eval/composed-score.mjs rewrite --kind K4 --mode sentence): the share of clean sentences changed is at most that of iteration 2 (1.4%); bad sentences fixed and wrongly rewritten are reported against iteration 2, iteration 1, the untrained base and no rewrite.
hypotheses.non_claim: Not a claim about SymbolicProofingLLM or about real user text. DeepSeek-written targets and the LLM judges are unreviewed and correlated; the meaning judge is calibrated on English originals only. A target word of the vocabulary probes is one of several valid translations (for instance Romanian "proprietar" is "landlord" or "owner"), so the word-kept rate undercounts correct paraphrases equally for every arm.

arms.name: language-proofing-gemma270m-it2 (iteration 2, epoch 3; the chat entry at the start of this run)

changed_factor: The training data only: iteration-2 data plus parts 010-025 (proofing-v3, 61,693 pairs), plus the reserve pairs of the ten formerly held-out words (1,258 after removing source rows and targets shared with the trained-vocabulary dev), minus every pair that contains one of eight NEW held-out words (1,772), plus spacing repair pairs (863 identity pairs with a spacing defect converted to repair pairs, 1,800 deterministic perturbations of clean identity sentences, 40 repair pairs dropped for a defective target). Same base, same recipe (LoRA r16 alpha32, lr 2e-4, batch 2 x 8, 3 epochs, seed 42), same prompt (message only), trained from the BASE. Note that "more data" (62,939 vs 36,915 pairs) and "the ten words in the data" are one factor here; the separate vocabulary effect is read from the two held-out probes of the SAME model, not from the comparison of runs.

recipe_policy.mode: LoRA adapter rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 2e-4, batch 2 x accumulation 8, max_length 8192, sdpa, bf16, seed 42, 3 epochs (config/train-gemma.json, unchanged)
recipe_policy.snapshots: one adapter snapshot per epoch (epoch-N, role proofreader), merged with training/python/merge.py for decoding

data.builder: tools/datasets/build-language-proofing-v3.mjs (from the qualified datasets/bad_english/proofing-v3; spacing rules tools/datasets/language-proofing/spacing.mjs; word lists tools/datasets/language-proofing/vocab-it3.mjs)
data.training_input: datasets/bad_english/proofing-it3/proofreader/{train,dev}.jsonl ({id, prompt, target, kind repair|identity, language_kind, target_source}), prompt_profile message-only

selection.rule: epoch snapshot selected on dev only, never on sealed data: among epochs whose identity-untouched rate on the dev identity units WITHOUT a spacing defect is at least 95% and whose mash-unchanged rate is at least 90%, the highest mean of the mechanical composite (clean-English gate AND content preserved) on devbg, heldout (trained vocabulary) and heldout-v3 (new probe) and a spacing exact-match rate of at least 80% on dev-spacing; ties by chrF on devbg, then lowest dev loss. The identity rate is computed without defect units because iteration 3 intentionally repairs spacing (the 115 dev identity units with a defect keep their old identity target).
selection.dev_decode_per_epoch: merge the epoch adapter (training/python/merge.py), greedy HF bf16 decode of dev2300 (stratified 300), devbg, heldout, heldout3, heldout3id, spacing and mash with tools/eval/language-proofing-eval.mjs generate, scores with `score`, held-out words with tools/eval/language-proofing-v3-metrics.mjs.

early_stopping.stop_rules: Stop training and keep the previous epoch if: more than 20% of dev outputs empty or length-capped; identity collapse (defect-free identity units changed in more than 10% after epoch 2); every repair output equals its input after epoch 1; non-finite loss, OOM, host available RAM below the 16 GiB floor, wall-time cap 240 minutes. Plateau stop when dev loss has not improved for 2 consecutive epochs. No stop is made for a poor held-out score alone (it is the measurement).
early_stopping.evaluation_stages: Stage 1: mechanical layer (clean-English gate, content preserved with negation, chrF, word kept, identity, mash, spacing exact match, child probe) on every dev and sealed unit, no judge. Stage 2: composed K4 sendAll with llama.cpp Q8_0 in stages of 100 and 300 sentences, then full, with the paired interval after each stage. Stage 3: LLM judges only on units whose iteration-3 output text differs from every earlier verdict (verdicts are keyed by text; identical outputs reuse the iteration-2 verdicts). Stop rules: a stage ends the evaluation early when the switch rule is already decided: (a) a catastrophic error class (child probe above 1%, mash or clean900 worse beyond the interval) decides "keep iteration 2" and the judge stage is skipped; (b) the trained-vocabulary criterion alone already has a paired interval above 0 together with the other gates, which decides "switch" and the composite judge stage is run only to report the composite, not to decide; (c) condition broken: more than 20% unparsable or empty outputs on the first 100 units.

judging.routing: owner routing 2026-10-01 (journal 02:57Z): mechanical checks and the local analysis gate (Stanza trees) first; the meaning judge is Grok (omp --model xai-oauth/grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, calibrated two-vote raw precision 99.0%, recall 76.5%, two votes m1 and m2 as in iteration 2); the parse judge is GLM (omp --model zai/glm-5.3-flash, most accurate but slow) or DeepSeek when time matters; fall back to DeepSeek only when a subscription errors. Every judge runs as an omp task folder under datasets_sources/, fenced and detached. The judging cost (items, tokens or calls, wall time) is reported.

chat_switch_rule: config/formalizers.json entry language-proofing-llm is switched to the iteration-3 GGUF if ALL hold: (1) no new catastrophic error class: child probe at most 1% and the mash-unchanged and clean900-untouched rates not worse than iteration 2 beyond their paired 95% intervals; (2) clean900 untouched of iteration 3 is at least that of iteration 2 (point estimate); (3) EITHER the composite on the judged sample OR the trained-vocabulary accuracy (target-word rate on dev-heldout, H1) improves over iteration 2 with a paired bootstrap 95% interval above 0. Otherwise the chat stays on iteration 2. The decision is noted in the registry `note`; the iteration-2 files stay on disk.

evaluation.decoding: greedy, message-only prompt; HF bf16 (selection, sealed test) and llama.cpp Q8_0 (deployment form, composed K4, CPU speed; GGUF with the tokenizer.json recipe); HF vs llama.cpp greedy agreement on 50 rows.
evaluation.metrics: as iteration 2 (tools/eval/language-proofing-eval.mjs, language-proofing-v2-*.mjs): clean-English rate, content preserved, chrF and token F1, analysis gate, identity untouched, two-vote meaning judge, composite = clean AND content AND analysis; plus the child probe, held-out word kept per word, mash unchanged, spacing exact match; Wilson and paired bootstrap 95% intervals (2,000 resamples).

non_goals: no change to SymbolicLM or lib/ud-to-sop rules; no tuning on any sealed file; no training of any model other than gemma-3-270m-it; no Gemma 3 1B (a 1B run needs its own preregistration and a plateau argument: this run is evidence for it only if the unseen-word failure is a capacity issue, which one run of 270M cannot show); no SOP-layer metric

deviations.what: The first per-epoch merge used the Python environment without peft and decoded nothing; the watcher was restarted with ~/proofreader-export-venv (CPU merge) and epoch 1 was decoded from the same checkpoint.
deviations.effect: none on training, data or selection

deviations.what: Iteration-2 outputs that differ from iteration-3 outputs on the judged sample (237 units) were judged again by the same Grok (meaning) and GLM (parse) judges that judged the new iteration-3 items, and iteration 2 is scored again as lp-it2-rj; the paired composite and meaning comparison use lp-it2-rj, the original DeepSeek-judged numbers are kept.
deviations.why: the calibrated judges differ in strictness (Grok recall 76.5%): comparing Grok verdicts of the new arm with DeepSeek verdicts of the old arm biased the meaning rate against iteration 3 by about 3 to 4 pp
deviations.effect: composite +0.0 [-3.2,+3.0] (re-judged) instead of +0.9 [-2.3,+4.0]; meaning +3.0 [-0.9,+6.8] instead of -4.0 [-7.6,-0.6]; the switch decision does not depend on it (the trained-vocabulary criterion carried it)

deviations.what: The eight held-out-v3 words are unseen only for iteration 3: iterations 1 and 2 had them in training (part of the pairs are literal it2 training pairs), so their rates on dev-heldout-v3 are seen-word rates.
deviations.why: the words were chosen from the v3 train vocabulary as the owner asked, and v3 contains the it2 train data
deviations.effect: H2 is evaluated on the it3 rate against its trained-vocabulary rate; it2 is reported as the seen reference, also on the 459 pairs that are not literal it2 training pairs

deviations.what: The first judge-item preparation ran without the iteration-3 folder variables and appended 214 parse and 320 meaning items to the iteration-1 judge folders; they were removed again (the input files hold exactly their earlier lines, the verdict files were never touched).
deviations.effect: none; items were rewritten into datasets_sources/language_proofing_it3_*

deviations.what: Epoch 2 was selected by the preregistered score (97.53) over epoch 3 (97.47); only epoch 2 was evaluated on sealed data.
deviations.effect: epoch 3 may be marginally better on chrF and mash (dev); not measured on sealed data

deviations.what: The trained-vocabulary accuracy of the switch rule is the target-word rate on dev-heldout (tools/eval/language-proofing-v3-metrics.mjs, first word of the list per row); the v2 tool that counts every root per row gives 45.8% for it2 and 93.8% for it3.
deviations.why: a per-row definition makes the paired bootstrap well defined
